commits.message:
[bugfix] Fix locale('__proto__') corrupting the global locale (#6442)

* Fix locale('__proto__') corrupting the global locale

The internal locale registry is a plain object, so loadLocale()
checked whether a locale was already loaded with locales[name] !== undefined.
For names like __proto__, constructor, or prototype, that lookup walks
the prototype chain and returns an inherited value instead of a real
locale entry, which then gets stored as the global locale and breaks
every later formatting call until a valid locale is set again.

Switch both lookups in loadLocale to hasOwnProp so an unrecognized
name is always treated as not found, the same way it would be for any
other unknown locale string.

* [bugfix] Guard locale fallback lookup

pulls.body:
From https://github.com/moment/moment/pull/5877

- Added correct translations for month names.
For example, ජනවාරි (pron. janawaari) and අගෝස්තු (pron. agoosthu) are loanwords.
See https://si.wikipedia.org/wiki/චන්ද්‍ර_මාස
See https://masteranylanguage.com/c/b/o9ly878fJ/98-Sinhala-MonthsOfYear-Learn-Step-By-Step

Note: Sinhala does not have standard abbreviations for month names, unlike English [locale/en-gb.js](https://github.com/moment/moment/blob/develop/src/locale/en-gb.js) which uses three-letter short forms (e.g., Jan, Feb). Shortening Sinhala month names changes their meanings entirely (for example, දුරු = cumin, නව = new, ඇස = eye). Sinhala month names lack standard abbreviations because the full names are already short enough.

- Corrected the translation of "minute" (මිනිත්තුව, pron. miniththuwa, a loanword).
- Corrected the translation of "Day" and "Days" to දවස and දවස් respectively (දිනය and දින mean "Date" and "Dates")

pulls.title: [bugfix] Fix floating point error in duration.as("weeks")
pulls.body:
`as('weeks')` is the only unit in `as()` that rounds twice: it divides the day part by 7 and the millisecond part by a week, then adds the two results. A duration that holds both days and milliseconds can therefore land one floating point step away from the exact value, as reported in #5851:

```js
moment.duration(1036800000).subtract(5, 'days').asWeeks(); // 0.9999999999999999
```

Every other unit multiplies an integer day count instead, so they stay exact for whole units. Adding the parts as milliseconds and dividing once returns 1 here, and clears the same off-by-a-step results for negative whole weeks.

The new test sits next to the existing issue #1867 assertions: it fails before the change (2 assertions) and passes after, and the full suite is green (3945 tests, 165046 assertions).

Closes #5851.

pulls.title: [bugfix] Parse the month format variant that object-shaped locales format with
pulls.body:
### Problem

`months` (and `monthsShort`) may be declared as an object with `standalone`, `format` and `isFormat`, so that a locale can write a different month form inside a longer format. That mechanism was added for the format side only (#3233): every parsing path still builds its month-name lists from `this.months(mom, '')` / `this.monthsShort(mom, '')`, which always resolve to the `standalone` list.

As a result, a locale that uses the `format` variant can no longer read back the output it produces, and in lenient mode it silently returns the wrong month:

```js
moment.locale('ca');
var s = moment([2024, 1, 14]).format('LL'); // '14 de febrer de 2024'
moment(s, 'LL', 'ca', true).isValid(); // false
moment(s, 'LL', 'ca').month(); // 0 -> January, silently wrong
```

Measured on `develop` (c2a703a) with `build/umd`:

| locale | path | `LL` output | strict parse | lenient parse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ca` | `monthsParseExact` | `14 de febrer de 2024` | invalid | month 0 |
| `oc-lnc` | `monthsParseExact` | `14 de febrièr de 2024` | invalid | month 0 |
| `be` | derived per-month regexes | `14 лютага 2024 г.` | invalid | month 1 only because the unanchored `^люты` regex happens to match the genitive prefix; `14 траўня…` (May) and `14 жніўня…` (August) are invalid |
| `lt` | derived per-month regexes | `2024 m. vasario 14 d.` | invalid | `rugpjūčio`, `rugsėjo` and `gruodžio` do not parse at all |

This is not a locale-data problem — the data is what CLDR describes for these languages (Catalan `LL` uses the `de <month>` partitive/prepositional form, Belarusian and Lithuanian use the genitive). It is the parsing code that ignores half of the locale's own declaration.

### Cause

Three places build parsing data from the standalone form only:

- `handleStrictParse()` (used when `monthsParseExact` is set) fills `_longMonthsParse`/`_shortMonthsParse` with `this.months(mom, '')`;
- `localeMonthsParse()` (the default path) builds the per-month regexes from `this.months(mom, '')` and `this.monthsShort(mom, '')`;
- `computeMonthsParse()` (which produces `_monthsRegex`, `_monthsStrictRegex` and the short equivalents that consume the `MMMM`/`MMM` token) pushes only `this.months(mom, '')` and `this.monthsShort(mom, '')`.

### Proposal

Feed the `format` list into those same three constructions, keeping the standalone list as the first thing tried so nothing that parses today changes:

- `monthFormatVariant()` returns `months.format[index]` when the locale declares an object-shaped list with an array `format`, and `null` for array-shaped or function-shaped lists;
- `handleStrictParse()` also stores the lower-cased format variants (in `_longMonthsFormatParse`/`_shortMonthsFormatParse`, registered in `monthsParseProperties` so `clearMonthsParseCache()` drops them with the rest of the derived caches) and looks them up after the standalone names;
- `localeMonthsParse()` appends the variants to the per-month regexes, with the existing `'^' + name` / `'$'` and `.replace('.', '')` handling preserved per name;
- `computeMonthsParse()` pushes the escaped variants into the same piece lists, which are already sorted longest-first so a longer variant wins over a shorter name that prefixes it.

Locales that ship their own `monthsParse`/`monthsRegex` (cs, ps, ru, es, nl, …) and locales whose `months` is a function (el, fi, hy-am, …) are untouched, because their parsing data is already supplied explicitly. Function-shaped lists cannot be enumerated, so inflected locales still need their own regexes — that is out of scope here.

### Tests

- `src/test/moment/locale.js`: a new case defines two locales, one with `monthsParseExact: true` and one on the default path, both with `months` and `monthsShort` object lists, and asserts all 12 months in both directions (standalone still parses, format variant parses strictly and leniently, `LL`/`ll` round trip).
- `src/test/locale/ca.js` and `src/test/locale/be.js`: round-trip `LL` for all 12 months, covering the two code paths with real locale data.

Results with these changes (Node 22, `node scripts/test.js`):

| check | without the fix | with the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--only=moment/locale` | 47 tests, 156 failed assertions | 47 tests, 0 failed |
| `--only=locale/ca` | 26 tests, 35 failed assertions | 26 tests, 0 failed |
| `--only=locale/be` | 27 tests, 26 failed assertions | 27 tests, 0 failed |
| full suite | 3947 tests, 165401 assertions, 3 failed tests, 217 failed assertions | 3947 tests, 165401 assertions, 0 failed |

`node_modules/.bin/eslint scripts src` and `node_modules/.bin/prettier --check src` are clean.

A side effect worth noting: a round-trip probe over all locales (139 locales, `L`/`LL`/`LLL`/`LLLL` formatted then parsed strictly) drops from 40 failures to 14, and the remaining ones are function-shaped `months` or unrelated tokens (weekday/separator handling), not the `format` variant.

No generated artifacts (`locale/`, `dist/`, `min/`, root `moment.js`) are included; `build/` output was only used locally to run the probes.

pulls.title: [bugfix] `duration.abs()`: preserve the interval of mixed-sign durations
pulls.body:
## Problem

`Duration.prototype.abs()` flips the sign of `_milliseconds`, `_days` and `_months` independently. For a duration that mixes signs, that changes the interval instead of only its direction:

```js
moment.duration(730.5, 'days').subtract(1, 'years').asDays(); // 365.5
moment.duration(730.5, 'days').subtract(1, 'years').abs().asDays(); // 1095.5
moment.duration(730.5, 'days').subtract(1, 'years').humanize(); // '3 years'
```

`humanize()` takes the absolute value of the duration internally, so the wrong interval and the wrong `'3 years'` also show up without an explicit `abs()` call. This is #4641, where @ichernev agreed that `abs` should "switch the signs if necessary" so the interval is preserved.

The same function also left the cached `days` value with its old sign, so `moment.duration(-14, 'days').abs().days()` returned `-14` (#4499).

## Fix

`abs()` now negates all three components together, and only when the duration as a whole is negative; it then rebuilds the `_data` cache with `_bubble()`. A positive duration is left untouched, so a mixed-sign interval no longer changes length, and a negative one keeps its relative signs while reporting a positive length.

## Tests

`src/test/moment/duration.js` covers the cached day/week getters after `abs()` for `-14`, `0` and `14` days (including idempotency and clone agreement) and for days bubbled from `-49` hours, plus the mixed-sign cases from #4641: one year expressed as days/years in both directions, `asDays()` and `humanize()` before and after `abs()`, and `-1 day + 2 hours`.

- Before the fix: the new duration assertions fail (`abs().asDays()` returns `1095.5`, `humanize()` returns `'3 years'`, and the cached `days()` stays negative).
- After the fix: `node scripts/test.js --only=moment/duration` is 55 tests / 1060 assertions with 0 failures; the full suite is 3947 tests / 165074 assertions with 0 failures; ESLint and Prettier are clean.

pulls.title: [bugfix] ug-cn: parse the meridiem and the long dates the locale writes
pulls.body:
### Bug

`ug-cn` cannot strictly parse its own afternoon output. A format/parse round trip
fails for every hour from 13:00 to 17:59:

```js
var format = 'YYYY-MM-DD h:mm:ss a';
var input = moment([2010, 1, 14, 15, 15, 0]).locale('ug-cn').format(format);
// '2010-02-14 3:15:00 چۈشتىن كېيىن'

moment(input, format, 'ug-cn'); // valid, hour 15
moment(input, format, 'ug-cn', true); // INVALID DATE
```

### Cause

`meridiemParse` lists the alternatives in the order the `meridiem()` function
happens to return them:

```js
meridiemParse: /يېرىم كېچە|سەھەر|چۈشتىن بۇرۇن|چۈش|چۈشتىن كېيىن|كەچ/
```

Regex alternation is ordered and matches at the earliest position, so at the start
of `چۈشتىن كېيىن` the shorter `چۈش` alternative wins and the longer afternoon form
is unreachable:

```
'چۈشتىن كېيىن'.match(/...|چۈش|چۈشتىن كېيىن|.../)[0] === 'چۈش'
```

The rest of the string is never consumed, and strict parsing rejects the input.
Lenient parsing hides the problem by ignoring the trailing text, and it only
produces a plausible hour by accident (`meridiemHour` falls through to the
`hour >= 11 ? hour : hour + 12` branch for the captured noon form).

### Fix

Order the alternatives longest-first so that no form is shadowed by a prefix of
itself. `چۈشتىن بۇرۇن` was already ahead of `چۈش`; only the afternoon form needs to
move. This is a parsing-only change: `meridiem()` output, `meridiemHour()` and all
formatting are untouched.

### Locale evidence

CLDR lists `چۈشتىن بۇرۇن` as the wide `am` form and `چۈشتىن كېيىن` as the wide `pm`
form for `ug`, so the afternoon form is the standard one that Moment already
formats with and must be able to parse:
[common/main/ug.xml#L1606-L1607](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/7afa5cdb6b7fe7ae65f934c6dbaa374f25b5a616/common/main/ug.xml#L1606-L1607)

### Tests

Added a `parse meridiem` test to `src/test/locale/ug-cn.js` that formats and
re-parses one timestamp per meridiem bucket (including both noon forms, which are
prefix-ambiguous) in strict and lenient mode, plus explicit assertions for the two
literal afternoon/noon strings.

Before the change (on this branch with only the test file added):

```
24 tests, 1096 assertions, 1 failed tests, 7 failed assertions
```

After the change:

```
24 tests, 1096 assertions, 0 failed tests, 0 failed assertions
```

Full suite and lint:

```
3945 tests, 165076 assertions, 0 failed tests, 0 failed assertions
eslint scripts src -> clean
prettier --check -> clean
```


---

## Second defect in the same locale: `LLL`/`LLLL` cannot be parsed back

`ug-cn` also rewrites its separator with a `preparse`/`postformat` pair:

```js
preparse: function (string) { return string.replace(/،/g, ','); },
postformat: function (string) { return string.replace(/,/g, '،'); },
```

`postformat` runs over the formatted result and `preparse` runs over the string being parsed, but the format *pattern* is never normalized. `LLL` and `LLLL` spell the separator as the Arabic comma (U+060C) directly, so a strict parse of a string the locale just wrote looks for `،` where `preparse` has already produced a plain `,`:

```js
moment.locale('ug-cn');
var s = moment([2024, 1, 14, 15, 25]).format('LLL'); // "2024-يىلى2-ئاينىڭ14-كۈنى، 15:25"
moment(s, 'LLL', 'ug-cn', true).isValid();           // false on develop
```

`parsingFlags()` reports the pattern's U+060C as an unused token and the U+002C that `preparse` produced as unused input, with `charsLeftOver: 1`. Lenient parsing papers over it.

The commit writes those two separators as plain commas, which `postformat` still renders as `،`, so the output does not change — the existing `format` test, which asserts the exact `LLL`/`LLLL` strings with the Arabic comma in them, keeps passing untouched. pulls.title: [locale] ga/mt: fix weekday name parsing and Maltese narrow names
pulls.body:
Two weekday-name bugs, one in `dddd` parsing and one in Maltese `dd` output.

### Full weekday names could not be parsed back (ga, mt)

Neither locale can read back its own full weekday names, because the default weekday matcher stops at the first word:

- `mt`: `moment('It-Tnejn', 'dddd', 'mt').isValid()` is false for all seven names.
- `ga`: worse, `moment('Dé Luain', 'dddd', 'ga').format('dddd')` gives `Déardaoin`, i.e. a Monday string silently becomes a Thursday (the `Dé` of the Thursday short/min form matches first).

Setting `weekdaysParseExact: true` fixes both; `ga` already does the same for months. I swept all 139 built locales, formatting each day of a week and parsing the result back with `dddd`: ga and mt are the only two that fail, so that is the whole scope.

### Maltese narrow names collided (mt)

`weekdaysMin` was `Ħa_Tn_Tl_Er_Ħa_Ġi_Si`: Thursday reused Sunday's `Ħa`, so `dd` produced only six distinct values and `moment('Ħa', 'dd', 'mt')` always meant Sunday. Thursday's own `dd` output round-tripped to Sunday:

| day | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sunday | `Ħa` → Sunday | `Ħd` → Sunday |
| Monday | `Tn` → Monday | `Tn` → Monday |
| Tuesday | `Tl` → Tuesday | `Tl` → Tuesday |
| Wednesday | `Er` → Wednesday | `Er` → Wednesday |
| Thursday | `Ħa` → **Sunday** | `Ħm` → Thursday |
| Friday | `Ġi` → Friday | `Ġm` → Friday |
| Saturday | `Si` → Saturday | `Sb` → Saturday |

The new values are CLDR's stand-alone narrow forms ([sun–sat, L149–L157](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/blob/a198dbf17e1d2314a76b84b30904b87a5f8618bb/cldr-json/cldr-dates-full/main/mt/ca-gregorian.json#L149-L157)), which also correct Sunday (`Ħd`, not `Ħa`), Friday (`Ġm`) and Saturday (`Sb`). CLDR's format-narrow set differs from this only in Monday (`T`); I kept the two-character stand-alone forms that `weekdaysMin` uses elsewhere.

### Tests

- New `format narrow week` test asserts all seven `dd` outputs plus a strict round-trip for each. On the first commit it fails 8 assertions (Sunday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday); it passes now.
- New `parse week` tests for ga and mt fail on develop (6 and 7 assertions).
- Full suite: 3947 tests / 165069 assertions, no failures; eslint, prettier and `check-months-parse` are clean.

### Use of AI

I used AI assistance to research the locale conventions and to check the change against CLDR; the behavior above was reproduced and tested locally.

pulls.title: [locale] gu: drop the stray viramas in October and Wednesday
pulls.body:
### Bug

The `gu` (Gujarati) locale spells October and Wednesday with a gujarati virama
(U+0ACD) where the word has no consonant cluster:

```js
moment([2024, 9, 16]).locale('gu').format('LLLL');
// 'બુધ્વાર, ૧૬ ઑક્ટ્બર ૨૦૨૪, રાત ૧૨:૦૦ વાગ્યે'
//   ↑ two broken names in one line
```

| field | in the locale today | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `months[9]` | `ઑક્ટ્બર` (…ટ + ્ + બર) | `ઑક્ટોબર` (…ટ + ો + બર) |
| `monthsShort[9]` | `ઑક્ટ્.` | `ઑક્ટો.` |
| `weekdays[3]` | `બુધ્વાર` (ધ + ્ + વાર) | `બુધવાર` |
| `weekdaysShort[3]` | `બુધ્` | `બુધ` |

A virama suppresses the inherent schwa of the consonant it follows, so
`બુધ્વાર` reads as a dead `d` before `vār`; the day is `બુધ` (Budha, Mercury) +
`વાર` with no conjunct, exactly like the other six names. `બુધ્વાર` is the only
weekday in the locale that puts a virama before `વાર`. For October the virama
stands in place of the `ઓ` vowel sign, so the stored form is not a spelling
variant of the word but the word with a hole in it.

### Cause

Four typos in the locale data, unchanged since the locale was added (#3796,
renamed from `gu-IN` in #4105). Nothing in
`src/lib` is involved — the names are read straight out of the arrays, and the
parse regexes are generated from them, so the same misspelling is both produced
and accepted today.

### Fix

Data-only: correct the four entries in `src/locale/gu.js`. No formatting logic,
no other field, and none of the neighbouring forms are touched.

### Evidence

- Unicode CLDR, Gujarati gregorian data:
  [October `ઑક્ટોબર`, L50](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/blob/a198dbf17e1d2314a76b84b30904b87a5f8618bb/cldr-json/cldr-dates-full/main/gu/ca-gregorian.json#L50)
  (format-wide) and
  [October short `ઑક્ટો`, L66](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/blob/a198dbf17e1d2314a76b84b30904b87a5f8618bb/cldr-json/cldr-dates-full/main/gu/ca-gregorian.json#L66),
  [Wednesday `બુધવાર`, L133](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/blob/a198dbf17e1d2314a76b84b30904b87a5f8618bb/cldr-json/cldr-dates-full/main/gu/ca-gregorian.json#L133)
  and
  [`બુધ`, L106](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json/blob/a198dbf17e1d2314a76b84b30904b87a5f8618bb/cldr-json/cldr-dates-full/main/gu/ca-gregorian.json#L106).
  The stand-alone copies agree (L94, L171). After the change, all 12 wide month
  names, all 7 wide weekday names and all 7 short weekday names equal the CLDR
  value, and the short month names differ only in the abbreviations and trailing
  periods the locale has always used.
- Official Gujarati-language usage from Gujarat state bodies uses `બુધવાર` and
  `ઑક્ટોબર`, e.g. the Personnel Department resolutions on the state e-Citizen
  portal («૩૧ ઑક્ટોબર, ૨૦૨૬ના રોજ સમગ્ર રાજ્યમાં રાષ્ટ્રીય એકતા દિવસની ઉજવણી…»,
  [gad.gujarat.gov.in government-resolutions-guj.htm](https://gad.gujarat.gov.in/personnel/government-resolutions-guj.htm)),
  the 2026 state holiday circular («બુધવાર, તારીખ ૧લી, એપ્રિલ, ૨૦૨૬»,
  [gmersmchvadnagar.com GovernmentHolidays2026.pdf](https://gmersmchvadnagar.com/Files/GovernmentHolidays2026.pdf))
  and Anand Agriculture University's circular of the same year
  («૧૮ ઑક્ટોબર ૨૦૨૫ … શનિવાર»,
  [new.aau.in circular PDF](http://new.aau.in/upload/circular/_%E0%AA%B8%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%95%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%B0_%E0%AA%A6%E0%AB%8D%E0%AA%B5%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%BE_%E0%AB%A8%E0%AB%A6%E0%AB%A8%E0%AB%AB%E0%AA%A8%E0%AA%BE_%E0%AA%B5%E0%AA%B0%E0%AB%8D%E0%AA%B7_%E0%AA%A6%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%AE%E0%AA%BF%E0%AA%AF%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%A8_%E0%AA%9C%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%B9%E0%AB%87%E0%AA%B0_%E0%AA%95%E0%AA%B0%E0%AB%87%E0%AA%B2_%E0%AA%B0%E0%AA%9C%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%93_%E0%AA%AC%E0%AA%BE%E0%AA%A4_Nov_24.pdf)).

pulls.title: [locale] el: parse the genitive month names the locale formats
pulls.body:
### Bug

The `el` locale formats month names in the genitive case whenever a day number
precedes them, but none of those genitive names can be parsed back. The locale
therefore writes dates that its own formats cannot read:

```js
const el = moment([2024, 1, 14]).locale('el');
const output = el.format('LL'); // '14 Φεβρουαρίου 2024'
moment(output, 'LL', 'el', true).isValid(); // false
moment('Μαΐου', 'MMMM', 'el').isValid(); // false — even the lenient parse fails
```

`LLLL` (`'Τετάρτη, 14 Φεβρουαρίου 2024 3:25 ΜΜ'`) and `LLL` fail the same way.
`Μαΐου` is worse than the rest: because the short form is `Μαϊ` (different
diacritic) the existing lenient prefix heuristic never matched it either, so the
genitive of May could not be parsed in any mode.

### Cause

`months` is a function that selects between `_monthsNominativeEl` and
`_monthsGenitiveEl`, so the default parse data compiled by
`src/lib/units/month.js` only ever sees the array returned for `months(mom, '')`
— the nominative one. The genitive forms are never registered in
`_monthsRegex`, `_monthsStrictRegex` or `_longMonthsParse`, and strict parsing
of anything the locale formats as a month fails.

### Fix

Register both cases in the locale's parse data, the same way `cs` (which also
declines its month names) already does: `monthsRegex`/`monthsShortRegex` accept
nominative + genitive + short, `monthsStrictRegex` accepts the two long cases,
`monthsShortStrictRegex` keeps the short forms only, and `monthsParse` resolves
the index for either case. Entries are ordered longest-first so that a short
form (`Ιουν`) can never shadow the genitive it prefixes (`Ιουνίου`).

No formatting data was touched, so no output changes.

### Evidence

- CLDR `el` lists the genitive as the *format*-context month name and the
  nominative as the *stand-alone* one:
  [common/main/el.xml L2107-L2109](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/7afa5cdb6b7fe7ae65f934c6dbaa374f25b5a616/common/main/el.xml#L2107-L2109)
  (`Ιανουαρίου`, `Φεβρουαρίου`) versus
  [L2151-L2153](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/7afa5cdb6b7fe7ae65f934c6dbaa374f25b5a616/common/main/el.xml#L2151-L2153)
  (`Ιανουάριος`, `Φεβρουάριος`). This is exactly the split the locale formats
  with, so both forms are in use and both need to parse.
- Official Greek institutional usage puts the genitive in dates, together with
  the weekday like `LLLL` does: the Hellenic Parliament proceedings open
  «Παρασκευή 15 Μαΐου 2020» —
  [hellenicparliament.gr es20200515.pdf](https://www.hellenicparliament.gr/UserFiles/a08fc2dd-61a9-4a83-b09a-09f4c564609d/es20200515.pdf).
- A secondary source on the convention, listing the genitive set used in dates
  (`Ιανουαρίου`, `Φεβρουαρίου`, …):
  [Reading Dates and Days of the Week in Greek](https://www.greekpod101.com/blog/2019-12-20/dates-in-greek/).

### Tests

`src/test/locale/el.js` gains two tests: one asserts that all 12 genitive names
parse with `MMMM` (lenient, strict and lower-cased strict), that the nominative
names still parse strictly, and that the short names still parse strictly with
`MMM`; the other round-trips `LL`, `LLL` and `LLLL` through a strict parse over
three dates.

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/test.js --only=locale/el` | 27 tests, 1205 assertions, **2 failed tests, 43 failed assertions** | 27 tests, 1205 assertions, 0 failed |
| full suite | 3946 tests, 165119 assertions, 0 failed | 3946 tests, 165119 assertions, 0 failed |
| `eslint` + `prettier --check` on both files | clean | clean |

I also diffed the behavior of the whole locale before and against the patched
build over every month name (both cases, short forms, upper/lower case), the
weekday names and 14 formats, plus long-date, calendar and meridiem output for
seven dates. The only differences are parses that used to be `INVALID`: the 12
genitive names with `MMMM`, and `Μαΐου` in the formats where it previously could
not be read at all. No formatted output differs.

A scratch round-trip check across all locales (format, then strict parse back)
drops the three `el` failures and introduces no new ones.

pulls.title: [locale] ur/sd: keep LLLL parseable through preparse
pulls.body:
### The bug

`ur` and `sd` rewrite the separator of their long dates with a `preparse`/`postformat` pair:

```js
preparse: function (string) { return string.replace(/،/g, ','); },
postformat: function (string) { return string.replace(/,/g, '،'); },
```

`postformat` runs over the formatted result and `preparse` runs over the string being parsed, but nothing normalizes the format *pattern* itself. Both locales spell the separator in `LLLL` as the Arabic comma (U+060C) directly:

```js
LLLL: 'dddd، D MMMM YYYY HH:mm',
```

So when a string the locale just wrote is parsed back strictly, `preparse` has already turned the `،` of the **input** into a plain `,` while the **pattern** still asks for `،`. The literal token never matches, strict mode records an unused token plus an unused input character, and the whole date is rejected:

```js
moment.locale('ur');
var s = moment([2024, 1, 14, 15, 25]).format('LLLL'); // "بدھ، 14 فروری 2024 15:25"
moment(s, 'LLLL', 'ur', true).isValid();              // false on develop
```

`parsingFlags()` for that call reports `unusedTokens: ["،"]`, `unusedInput` holding the U+002C that `preparse` produced, and `charsLeftOver: 1`. Lenient parsing papers over it, so this is the strict round trip of the locale's own output that breaks — exactly what `moment(string, format, locale, true)` is used for.

### The fix

Write the separator in the pattern the way the rest of the tree does — as a plain `,` — and let `postformat` render it:

```js
LLLL: 'dddd, D MMMM YYYY HH:mm',
```

The rendered output does not change: `format()` applies `localeData().postformat()` to the result, so the comma is still written as `،`, and both locales' existing `format` tests — which assert the exact string `اتوار، 14 فروری 2010 15:25` with U+060C in it — keep passing untouched. Only the internal representation of the pattern moves to the form `preparse` produces.

Why the pattern is the right side to change, not `preparse`:

* `ur` and `sd` are the only locales in `src/locale/` that put U+060C inside a `longDateFormat` pattern, and they are the only ones whose `preparse` rewrites that character; the two facts together make the pattern inconsistent with its own locale.
* Every other locale with a `preparse`/`postformat` pair that renders a comma writes a plain `,` in its patterns (`ps`: `dddd D, MMMM, YYYY [په] H:mm`, `fa`: `dddd, D MMMM YYYY HH:mm`), and those round trip strictly today.
* CLDR keeps the Arabic comma in the displayed Urdu full date (`EEEE، d MMMM، y` in `common/main/ur.xml`), which is what the output still is.

### Tests

Added `long dates round trip through a strict parse` to `src/test/locale/ur.js` and `src/test/locale/sd.js`: `LL`, `LLL` and `LLLL` are formatted for three dates, parsed back strictly with the same pattern and compared, and `LLLL` is asserted to keep the Arabic comma and never leak a plain `,`, so the visible separator is pinned too.

| command | before the locale change | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/test.js --only=locale/ur` | 1 failed test, 6 failed assertions | 24 tests, 990 assertions, 0 failed |
| `node scripts/test.js --only=locale/sd` | 1 failed test, 6 failed assertions | 24 tests, 990 assertions, 0 failed |
| `node scripts/test.js` | — | 3946 tests, 165081 assertions, 0 failed |

`eslint scripts src` and `prettier --check src` are clean. A sweep over every locale (`LT/LTS/L/LL/LLL/LLLL` formatted with the locale and parsed back strictly with the same pattern) loses the two `ur`/`sd` `LLLL` entries with this change and nothing else.

### Related

`ug-cn` has the same mismatch in its `LLL`/`LLLL` patterns. I am keeping it in a separate pull request so that the two changes do not collide on the same files.

pulls.title: [bugfix] day()/isoWeekday(): keep the date when the weekday name is unparsable
pulls.body:
`parseWeekday()` returns `null` for a name it doesn't recognize, and `day()` used that `null` as a day number, so the moment silently jumped back to the start of the week:

```js
moment('2020-06-15').day('xyz').format('YYYY-MM-DD');         // 2020-06-14, expected 2020-06-15
moment('2020-06-15').isoWeekday('xyz').format('YYYY-MM-DD');  // 2020-06-21
moment('2020-06-15').isoWeekday(NaN);                         // returns a number, so chaining breaks
```

`month()` already treats an unparsable name as a no-op (`setMonth` returns the moment unchanged), so this makes the two weekday setters follow the same rule.

The existing `day(0).day('invalid').day() === 0` assertion stays green; it only passed because that moment started on a Sunday. Added assertions use a Monday so a wrong shift can't hide.

Ran the whole suite here: 3944 tests / 165046 assertions, nothing failed; eslint and prettier clean.

pulls.title: [feature] Add internal date-default hook for Moment Timezone
pulls.body:
## Summary

Adds an internal `moment._getDefaultDateParts(config, now, forWeek)` hook that extensions can use to supply the year, month, and date for omitted calendar fields.

This is needed by Moment Timezone so parsing inputs such as time-only strings can default to the current calendar date in the configured default timezone rather than the host system timezone.

The hook is intentionally private and is not included in the TypeScript declarations.

Moment's default implementation preserves existing local and UTC behavior.

- Supports locale and ISO week-based parsing.
- Preserves `moment.updateOffset` behavior when calculating week defaults.
- Samples `moment.now()` lazily and only once across format-array candidates.
- Avoids sampling the current time for complete calendar dates.
- Preserves day-of-year precedence for formats containing both calendar and ordinal dates.

There should be no behavior change unless an extension overrides the private hook.

## Related issue

Supports the Moment Timezone fix for moment/moment-timezone#1160.

## Testing

- Local and UTC default date parts.
- Locale and ISO week defaults.
- Explicit-offset week parsing.
- Two-argument hook wrappers.
- `updateOffset` integration.
- Format-array clock consistency.
- Complete dates with `DDD` and `DDDD`.

pulls.title: [bugfix] Fix locale('__proto__') corrupting the global locale
pulls.body:
Reported in #6440. `loadLocale()` checks whether a name is already loaded with `locales[name] !== undefined`, and since `locales` is a plain object, that lookup falls through to `Object.prototype` for names like `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. The result then gets assigned as the global locale by `getSetGlobalLocale`, and every later call to `format`/`calendar`/`fromNow` throws because `Object.prototype` obviously isn't a real `Locale`.

Repro against current develop:

```js
const moment = require('moment');
moment.locale('__proto__');
moment().format('LLLL'); // TypeError: locale.longDateFormat is not a function
```

The fix swaps both lookups in `loadLocale` to use the existing `hasOwnProp` helper (already used elsewhere in this file) instead of a plain property check, so an own-property-only lookup treats these names the same as any other locale that was never registered: not found, warn, keep the current locale.

Added a regression test in `src/test/moment/locale.js` covering `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`, and `toString`. Ran `pnpm validate` (lint + full suite, 3930 tests / 164926 assertions) clean.

pulls.title: [bugfix] weekday mismatch when the format only has part of a date
pulls.body:
Fixes #6228

Parsing a weekday together with an incomplete date gives back an invalid moment:

    moment('Sat 10', 'ddd DD').isValid()  // false
    moment('Sat 01', 'ddd MM').isValid()  // false

while 'ddd', 'DD' and 'ddd YYYY' on their own all parse fine. That means
format() and then parse with the same format does not round trip, which is
how the issue was found.

The cause is in configFromArray. The parsed weekday is only used to build a
date when neither day of month nor month was parsed. With 'ddd DD' the day
of month is set, so the weekday never contributes anything, the year and
month quietly default to today, and then the weekday gets compared against
whatever date those defaults produced. Today is August, day 10 is a Monday,
so 'Sat 10' is reported as a mismatch. The result also depends on the day
you run it, which is why 'Mon 10' happens to work right now.

The fix records whether any of year, month or day of month had to be filled
in from the current date, and only runs the mismatch check when the whole
date actually came from the input. A weekday cannot contradict a value the
user never supplied.

Behavior that people rely on is unchanged. A full date with the wrong
weekday is still rejected:

    moment('Wed 08-10-2017', 'ddd MM-DD-YYYY').isValid()  // false
    moment('Thu 08-10-2017', 'ddd MM-DD-YYYY').isValid()  // true

The invalidWeekday flag is a separate thing and is untouched, so
moment('a', 'ddd') is still invalid. Week based formats such as
'gggg ww e' and 'GGGG [W]WW E' go through the day of year path before the
snapshot is taken, so they are unaffected.

To check for regressions beyond the suite I diffed the released build
against the patched source over 23 formats crossed with 25 inputs in both
strict and non strict mode, 1150 cases. There were 63 differences and every
one of them went from invalid to valid. Nothing went the other way, and no
moment that was already valid changed its parsed value. The only visible
change is that input which used to be rejected now parses.

Tests: added two cases to src/test/moment/parsing_flags.js. One walks all
seven weekdays across 'ddd DD', 'ddd MM' and 'ddd MM-DD' and asserts no
mismatch flag and a valid moment. The other is the round trip from the
issue report. Full suite passes, 3911 tests and 164038 assertions with no
failures. eslint and prettier are clean.

issues.title: [Bug] moment(isoString) converts the embedded UTC offset to defaultZone in 2.31.0 when moment.tz.setDefault(zone) is active
issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I read the applicable [documentation](https://momentjs.com/docs/) and [guides](https://momentjs.com/guides/).
- [x] I reproduced the problem with the latest Moment.js release.
- [x] I confirmed this belongs to Moment.js core, not [Moment Timezone](https://github.com/moment/moment-timezone/issues), [Luxon](https://github.com/moment/luxon/issues), or the [momentjs.com website](https://github.com/moment/momentjs.com/issues).

### Description

I've observed different behaviour of `moment(isoString)` between 2.29.4 and 2.31.0, which was not documented, but it looks like breaking change

## Commit that introduced the breaking change

**[`710703b`](https://github.com/moment/moment/commit/710703b7eac93535ad125cbf4feb3d42afed6fb3)** — *[feature] Add internal date-default hook for Moment Timezone ([#6451](https://github.com/moment/moment/pull/6451))*  
Author: Matt Johnson-Pint · Merged: 2026-09-14 · Shipped in: **2.31.0**

The companion moment-timezone PR that activates the hook is **[moment/moment-timezone#1161](https://github.com/moment/moment-timezone/pull/1161)** — both were merged on the same day and both are required for the behaviour change.

---

## Exact files and lines

| File | Lines | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| [`src/lib/create/from-array.js`](https://github.com/moment/moment/commit/710703b7eac93535ad125cbf4feb3d42afed6fb3#diff-...) | ~19–112 | `currentDateArray()` now delegates to `hooks._getDefaultDateParts()` which moment-timezone overrides |
| `moment-timezone.js` (0.5.37) | **605–628** | `moment.updateOffset()` — runs on every new moment, re-converts it to `defaultZone` |
| `moment-timezone.js` (0.5.37) | **543–546** | `needsOffset()` guard: `return !!(m._a && (m._tzm === undefined) && !isUnixTimestamp)` — in practice `_tzm` is set for explicit-offset ISO strings but `updateOffset` at line 610 still fires due to `mom._z === undefined` |

---

## Live reproduction (verified)

```js
const moment = require('moment');
require('moment-timezone');

moment.tz.setDefault('Asia/Tokyo');  // UTC+9

const iso = '2015-09-19T06:31:44.000+00:00';  // explicit +00:00

moment(iso).format('HH:mm:ss');
// 2.29.4 → '06:31:44'  ✅
// 2.31.0 → '15:31:44'  ❌  (+9 h shift)

moment.parseZone(iso).format('HH:mm:ss');
// 2.31.0 → '06:31:44'  ✅  workaround

moment.tz.setDefault();
```

Ran this exact script against moment **2.31.0** + moment-timezone **0.5.37** in this repo and confirmed the output.

---

## Key mechanics

The issue is in **moment-timezone's `updateOffset`** ([line 605–628 of `moment-timezone.js`](https://github.com/moment/moment-timezone/blob/master/moment-timezone.js#L605)). It fires on every newly-constructed moment. The guard `needsOffset(m)` checks `m._tzm === undefined` — but `_tzm` is only set reliably via the `Z`/`ZZ` token in a *format string* (`moment(str, fmt)`). When you call bare `moment(isoString)`, Moment's ISO auto-parser sets `_pf.tzm` internally but the `_tzm` property on the moment instance isn't populated the same way, so the `needsOffset` guard doesn't block the re-conversion.



### Minimal reproduction

```javascript
const moment = require('moment');
require('moment-timezone');

moment.tz.setDefault('Asia/Tokyo');  // UTC+9

const iso = '2015-09-19T06:31:44.000+00:00';  // explicit +00:00

moment(iso).format('HH:mm:ss');
// 2.29.4 → '06:31:44'  ✅
// 2.31.0 → '15:31:44'  ❌  (+9 h shift)

moment.parseZone(iso).format('HH:mm:ss');
// 2.31.0 → '06:31:44'  ✅  workaround

moment.tz.setDefault();
```

_No response_

### Actual behavior

See above, different output produced between 2.94.4 and 2.31.0

### Expected behavior

The output value will be same as on 2.29.4 or new behaviour will be documented as breaking change with recommended work-around

### Moment.js version

2.31.0

### Runtime

Nodejs 22.23.3

### Loading method

ESM bundle, npm CommonJS

### Locale

not applicable

### Time zone

any timezone different than UTC e.g. Asia/Tokyo

issues.title: [Bug] Timezone offset is not range-validated: isValid() stays true for out-of-range offsets
issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I read the applicable documentation and guides.
- [x] I reproduced the problem with the latest Moment.js release.
- [x] I confirmed this belongs to Moment.js core, not Moment Timezone, Luxon, or the momentjs.com website.

### Description

Moment.js does not validate that a timezone offset parsed from an ISO-8601 string, or passed numerically to `utcOffset()`, falls within the real world range of `-12:00` to `+14:00`. The hour and minute groups each accept any two digits (`00`-`99`), so the offset can reach 6039 minutes (about 4.19 days), and `isValid()` returns `true` for it, including in strict mode. Separately, `utcOffset(number)` infers hours vs minutes from the magnitude (`|input| < 16` is treated as hours), so two adjacent integers land far apart.

### Minimal reproduction

```javascript
const moment = require('moment'); // 2.30.1

// Out-of-range offset in an ISO string
const m = moment('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99');
console.log(m.isValid());     // true
console.log(m.toISOString()); // 2026-08-28T19:21:00.000Z

// Strict mode does not catch it either
console.log(moment('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99', moment.ISO_8601, true).isValid()); // true
console.log(moment.parseZone('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99').utcOffset());            // 6039

// Magnitude-based hours/minutes inference
console.log(moment().utcOffset(15).format('Z')); // +15:00
console.log(moment().utcOffset(16).format('Z')); // +00:16
```

### Actual behavior

```
true
2026-08-28T19:21:00.000Z
true
6039
+15:00
+00:16
```

`isValid()` is `true` for `+99:99`, and the parsed instant is silently shifted back about 4 days 4 hours 39 minutes. `utcOffset(15)` and `utcOffset(16)` differ by 14.7 hours.

### Expected behavior

An offset outside `-12:00`..`+14:00` should make `isValid()` return `false` (at least in strict mode), consistent with how other out-of-range fields are handled by `checkOverflow`. `utcOffset(15)` vs `utcOffset(16)` should not silently switch unit interpretation without a warning.

### Moment.js version

2.30.1

### Runtime

Node.js 24.16.0

### Loading method

npm CommonJS

### Locale

not applicable

### Time zone

not applicable (offset supplied in the input string)

### Additional context

Root cause:
- `src/lib/units/offset.js` `offsetFromString()` computes `minutes = parts[1] * 60 + parts[2]` with no bound on either group.
- The offset-matching regex (`matchShortOffset` / `matchOffset`) accepts `[+-]\d\d(?::?\d\d)?`.
- `src/lib/create/from-array.js` `checkOverflow()` validates Y/M/D/H/m/s/ms but never inspects `config._tzm`, so an out-of-range offset never flips `isValid()` to false, even in strict mode.
- `getSetOffset()` infers offset units from magnitude rather than an explicit flag.

Possible fix directions: range-check the offset in `offsetFromString()`, tighten the offset regex to the legal range (e.g. `[+-](?:0\d|1[0-4])(?::?[0-5]\d)?`), add `_tzm` to `checkOverflow()`, and consider deprecating the magnitude-based unit inference.

issues.title: [Bug] moment.locale('__proto__') corrupts the global locale and breaks formatting
issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I read the applicable documentation and guides.
- [x] I reproduced the problem with the latest Moment.js release.
- [x] I confirmed this belongs to Moment.js core, not Moment Timezone, Luxon, or the momentjs.com website.

### Description

The internal locale registry is a plain object (`var locales = {}`), and `loadLocale(name)` decides a locale is already loaded with `if (locales[name] !== undefined)`. For the name `__proto__`, `locales['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` through the built-in `__proto__` accessor, which is not `undefined`, so `loadLocale` returns `Object.prototype` before the `isLocaleNameSane` check ever runs. `getSetGlobalLocale` then stores that value as the global locale with no `instanceof Locale` check, and every later formatting call throws because `Object.prototype` has none of the `Locale` methods. The global locale stays corrupted until it is set again explicitly. `constructor` and `prototype` reach the same code path.

### Minimal reproduction

```javascript
const moment = require('moment'); // 2.30.1

console.log(moment.locale());       // en
moment.locale('__proto__');
console.log(moment.locale());       // undefined
console.log(moment().format('LLLL')); // throws
```

### Actual behavior

```
en
undefined
TypeError: locale.longDateFormat is not a function
```

After `moment.locale('__proto__')`, `moment.locale()` returns `undefined` and every locale-dependent formatting call (`format` with locale tokens, `calendar()`, `fromNow()`) throws for the rest of the process, until `moment.locale('en')` (or another valid locale) is set again.

### Expected behavior

An unrecognized locale name, including `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`, should be treated as "not found" (warn and keep the current locale), exactly like any other unknown name. It should never replace the global locale with a non-`Locale` value.

### Moment.js version

2.30.1

### Runtime

Node.js 22.x and 24.x

### Loading method

npm CommonJS

### Locale

not applicable

### Time zone

not applicable

### Additional context

Root cause:
- `src/lib/locale/locales.js` declares `var locales = {}` (and `localeFamilies = {}`) as plain objects, so property lookups fall through to `Object.prototype`.
- `loadLocale()` uses `if (locales[name] !== undefined)` before `isLocaleNameSane`, so `__proto__` returns `Object.prototype` and short-circuits.
- `getSetGlobalLocale()` assigns any truthy `getLocale()` result to the global locale without an `instanceof Locale` check.

Possible fix directions: use `Object.create(null)` for the registries, replace `locales[name] !== undefined` with an explicit `hasOwnProp(locales, name)` check, run `isLocaleNameSane` (extended to reject `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`) before any `locales[...]` access, and require `instanceof Locale` in `getSetGlobalLocale` before assigning the global locale.

Reported by @manqingzhou. Thanks for the analysis and reproduction.

issues.title: [Analysis] Issue Backlog Health Check: 46+ bugs open from pre-2023, 1 bug fixed in ~20 months — the "maintenance mode" gap
issues.body:
# Bug Backlog Analysis: Moment.js Issue Tracker Health (September 2026)

## Overview

This issue presents a quantitative analysis of the Moment.js issue tracker, examining the gap between incoming bug reports and resolution velocity. The data reveals a significant and growing backlog — one that the "maintenance mode" status alone does not fully account for.

---

## Key Metrics

### Aging Open Issues
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Open issues created **before 2023** | **46** |
| Open issues created **before 2020** | **~25** |
| Oldest open bug (still relevant) | [#2928](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/2928) — Jan 2016 (10+ years) |
| Bugs labeled "Bug" still open | **5** |
| Bugs with other issue-type labels (DST, Duration, etc.) still open | **~45** |
| Open issues from 2025+ | **3** |

### Resolution Rate (2025–2026)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total issues closed in 2025–2026 | **36** |
| Actual bug fixes among those closures | **~1** (#6295, closed July 2026) |
| Spam / invalid / non-bug closures | **~30** (e.g., #6334, #6332, #6340, #6342 — spam, bounty pitches, off-topic) |
| Genuine bug reports closed as completed | **~1** |
| **Effective bug resolution rate** | **~1 bug fixed in ~20 months** |

### The "Known Issue" Label Pattern
Multiple significant bugs have been labeled `Known Issue` — a label whose description references issue #6373 (now deleted/private) — effectively acknowledging them without any plan for resolution:

- [#5515](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/5515): Different `utcOffset()` results in Firefox vs Chrome — "Known Issue"
- Several other DST and fractional-offset issues are similarly labeled

---

## Specific Long-Standing Bugs (with Details)

### 1. [#2928](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/2928) — Duration days inconsistent (Bug, Duration bubble issues)
- **Opened:** January 28, **2016** (over 10 years)
- **Author:** @juhamust
- **Summary:** `moment.duration(0.123, 'years').days()` returns `0`, but `moment.duration(0.123 * 365, 'days').days()` returns `~13.89`
- **Comments:** 6 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, last update May 2020

### 2. [#3706](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/3706) — `.startOf("hour")` wrong across DST boundaries (Bug, DST)
- **Opened:** January 6, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @colinhunt
- **Summary:** `moment.tz("2017-04-02T01:30:00+10:30", "Australia/Lord_Howe").startOf("hour")` returns `01:30+11:00` instead of `01:00+11:00`
- **Comments:** 1 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, updated Aug 2026

### 3. [#3980](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/3980) — Incorrect month diff when time involved (Bug)
- **Opened:** May 26, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @standy
- **Summary:** `b.diff(a, 'M')` where b > c produces transitivity violation: `c - a` should be ≥ `b - a` but is 0 vs 1
- **Comments:** 5 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, updated Sept 2026

### 4. [#4127](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/4127) — from()/to() wrong days calculation around month boundary (Bug)
- **Opened:** August 17, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @pretender
- **Summary:** `now.to(expiredAt)` and `tomorrow.to(expiredAt)` both return `'30 days ago'` despite being a full day apart
- **Comments:** 5 | **Reactions:** 👍 2
- **Status:** Still open, updated Sept 2026

### 5. [#5515](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/5515) — Different `utcOffset()` in Firefox vs Chrome (Known Issue)
- **Opened:** May 6, **2020** (over 6 years)
- **Author:** @heroboy
- **Summary:** Historical dates produce different UTC offsets across browsers (486 min in Chrome, -485.7 min in Firefox for the same date)
- **Comments:** 6 | **Reactions:** 👍 1
- **Status:** Still open, labeled "Known Issue", updated Sept 2026

### 6. [#6440](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/6440) — `moment.locale('__proto__')` corrupts global locale
- **Opened:** September 4, **2026** (new but critical)
- **Author:** @UlisesGascon
- **Summary:** Passing `'__proto__'` to `moment.locale()` corrupts the global locale object and breaks formatting
- **Comments:** 0 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Fresh, no response yet

---

## Patterns Observed

### 1. Single-Point-of-Failure Maintainer Model
The commit history shows that essentially all recent commits (Aug–Sept 2026) are from a single contributor (@mattjohnsonpint). While their work is high-quality and appreciated, this creates a bottleneck where one person's bandwidth determines the entire project's velocity.

### 2. "Maintenance Mode" as a De-Facto Freeze
The README declares "maintenance mode" and states "new features are not being accepted." However, in practice, even bug fixes are barely trickling through (1 bug fixed in ~20 months). The project is effectively in **life-support mode**, not maintenance mode.

### 3. Triage Without Resolution
Many issues have been triaged with labels like `Known Issue`, `Duration bubble issues`, `relative time threshold issues`, `Fractional-Hour UTC Offset` — these are effectively graveyards. They acknowledge the bug without any timeline, milestone, or assignee for resolution.

### 4. Disproportionate Spam Consumption
Of the 36 issues closed in 2025–2026, approximately 30 (~83%) were spam, off-topic, or invalid posts. This means the limited maintainer attention is disproportionately consumed by issue triage rather than actual fixes.

### 5. Massive User Base, Minimal Support
Moment.js still has:
- **~48,000 GitHub stars**
- **~12 million weekly npm downloads**
- Used in **~4 million+ dependent repositories**

This is an enormous user base relying on a library with effectively frozen bug resolution.

### 6. No Clear Migration Path Enforced
While the README recommends alternatives (Luxon, Day.js, date-fns, js-joda), there is no deprecation timeline, no runtime warnings encouraging migration, and no plan to actively guide the massive user base away.

---

## Recommendations

1. **Add deprecation warnings at runtime** — a non-breaking console.warn on `moment()` import that points users to alternatives
2. **Close or explicitly acknowledge all pre-2020 bugs** — if they won't be fixed, say so clearly and close them to reduce noise
3. **Invite more maintainers** — specifically for triage to filter spam and reduce the bottleneck on @mattjohnsonpint
4. **Create a migration guide** as a pinned issue — practical recipes for common Moment.js patterns in Luxon / Day.js / date-fns
5. **Consider archiving the repo** — if the project is truly in life-support mode, archiving with a clear sunset notice would be more honest to the community than the current state

---

*This analysis was compiled by examining the issue tracker on September 9, 2026, using GitHub's API. Data is publicly available and verifiable.*
